problems: OPEN, orchestrator: lohara-dynasty (and utpala-dynasty) still duplicate kashmir.json for 1003-1339; the merge needs edits to kashmir.json, which belongs to another sa-03 part. The steps are in history/polities/_notes/sa-03-g.md (Repair section) and in lohara-dynasty.json notes. lohara-dynasty now ends in 1339 to match kashmir.json and carries the Mongol vassal pair (1235 start, 1320 end), Rinchan and the Lohara return as renames, and the 1338-1339 Shah Mir war.

Vassal events are written from the vassal's side (counterpart = the suzerain) as the review asked, in lohara-dynasty (mongol-empire), sena-dynasty (pala-empire 1070-1095), eastern-ganga-kingdom (tughlaq-dynasty 1358-1359) and hoysala-kingdom (western-chalukya-empire 1122-1126, khalji-dynasty 1311-1318); the schema describes vassal events from the suzerain's side, so the suzerain dossiers (mongol-empire ia-02, pala-empire, tughlaq-dynasty and khalji-dynasty sa-04) should carry the mirror.

Mirror work for neighbour authors: pala-empire (drop Radha from its keyframes from 1095; dissolve 1161 against the Sena page's after-1165 annexation of Bihar); chola-empire (Ganga steps 1078/1102/1118/1126, Hoysala vassal 1220-1245 and losses 1225/1236, Vengi overlap with western-chalukya-empire c. 1118); western-chalukya-empire (Hoysala Banavasi/Humacha 1120 and Hanagal/Uchchangi/Bankapura 1140 losses, the Someshvara VI rump after 1187); yadava-dynasty (1192 loss and 1212 gain with hoysala-kingdom); pandya-empire (1263 gain and c. 1295 loss of the Tamil holdings); mamluk-dynasty (Rarh occupation 1244-1247); gurjara-pratihara-dynasty /ledger/38 (1036 dissolve to a state that starts in 1085); kara-khitans /ledger/12 (Pamir cells to lohara-dynasty should go to nobody); kamarupa-kingdom /ledger/25 (32 cells to the Senas in 1072); chandela-kingdom /ledger/9 (1085 loss to the Gahadavalas, not on the Gahadavala page).

Beyond the reviewer's options: eastern-ganga-kingdom Sambalpur is a contest pair 1150-1156 plus a gain in 1211 (the Eastern Ganga page gives the conquest to Anangabhima III); gahadavala-dynasty stages the 1085 shape (Varanasi, Ayodhya 1090, Kannauj 1093, a confidence-1 bridge c. 1100) because the 1090 and 1093 dates are inscription attestations; a reader preferring the whole outline from 1085 can drop those events and keyframes.

Kept against the review's suggestion: sena-dynasty 1159 Gaur gain not moved into Vijaya Sena's reign (the pages contradict each other); eastern-ganga-kingdom Vengi counterpart stays chola-empire (the Chodaganga page names Vikrama Chola). Both are explained in the dossier notes.

Pages re-read with WebFetch (all already in the dossiers' sources, so no source added and no page budget exceeded): Kashmir Sultanate, Lohara dynasty, Eastern Ganga dynasty (three times), Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva, Kulottunga Chola I, Narasingha Deva I, Sena dynasty, Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji, Vijaya Sena, Govindachandra (Gahadavala dynasty), Gahadavala dynasty, Veera Ballala II, Veera Ballala III, Hoysala Empire, Vira Someshwara, Vishnuvardhana. WebFetch returns extracts and paraphrases, so quotes are as returned.
